plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes public K-12 schools in Alabama to form volunteer emergency security forces composed of current/retired school employees and local citizens.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would allow principals or superintendents to request volunteers when student safety is deemed inadequate. Once a sufficient number of suitable volunteers are identified by the sheriff or chief of police, an emergency security force program can be initiated for that specific school. These volunteers serve as reserve deputy sheriffs or reserve police officers under the supervision and direction of local law enforcement but do not possess arrest powers.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Morrow (RFD: Education Policy) sponsored this bill to establish a mechanism for enhanced school security through volunteer forces supervised by local law enforcement.
evidence_quotes: This bill would authorize the formation of volunteer emergency security forces at public K-12 schools in the state consisting of current and retired school employees and local citizens.

Once a list of volunteers has been compiled, the principal or the local superintendent of education shall submit the list to the local sheriff or chief of police... If the sheriff or chief of police determines the number of suitable volunteers is sufficient, he or she may initiate an emergency security force program for the school.

A volunteer emergency security force member shall be classified as a reserve deputy sheriff or reserve police officer and shall serve in that position at the pleasure of the sheriff or chief of police. Service as a reserve deputy sheriff or reserve police officer under this section shall not include the power of arrest.
